Fe yu ke ri di yu ke ta Esata

If you can read this you can talk Esata.

I discovered Esata when browsing the conlangs on Verbix and I find it most interesting. Rather than proclaiming itself to be the next international language, instead it plays off of English's unofficial lingua franca status and creates an "official" English creole.

Here's the creator's website: http://www.beginnersgame.com/esata.html

You can also find a grammar book PDF for it on there.

Its weird how common words are condensed into mere syllables, it reminds me of Japanese. Weird, yet satisfying. Unfortunately Esata has hardly been touched; I even searched through Reddit and saw no mention of it. Perhaps us Goatees should give it a try?
Never heard of it. It felt satisfying that except for the word 'ta' or 'talk' I could understand that sentence almost instantly.
I think why its ta rather than anything else is because multi-consonant spelling is not used. Speak would have to be Spi, but it can't be. Also Si and Pi are probably used by something else.
The effort that went into creating this language (a 125 page report), and from a quick browse many other languages, is insane compared to the actual use of them.
I'm impressed by the sheer ingenuity. I've always fantasized of rewriting the English language to be easier and more phonetic, but Esata has outdone anything that I could have thought of.
